bullets.title: Joule Sous vide device
bullets.note:
I used this elegant device to cook Valentine’s Day dinner not long ago. It was
developed by ChefSteps, a company co-founded by podcast guest Chris Young
([Lessons from Geniuses, Billionaires, and
Tinkerers](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=d8z&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=L&)).
Here’s how it works, using meat as an example: “Put the Joule in a pot with
some water and pick your temp in the app [they have many fool-proof recipes].
Then, put your food in a ziplock-style bag (season or marinate as you wish)
and drop it in the water. While you wait, pour a drink, chat with guests, or
crush some fancy sides. Then, right before serving, finish with a quick sear
for a crispy crust. The result? The juiciest, most tender meat in the history
of Chez You.” It can be used for veggies, eggs, and just about anything. In my
case, I cooked some delicious grass-fed yak sent to me by renowned strength
coach [Charles
Poliquin](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=d8B&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=6&)
(thanks, Charles!).

bullets.title: Rubz
bullets.note:
Meet my newest travel partner, which can be thought of as a golf ball that
won’t shoot across the floor when stepped on. Roll this uniquely designed ball
under your feet (my go-to area) or over any sore or tired muscle to reduce
tension. It’s small enough to fit in a pocket and easy to manipulate.
